prompt: You denied the prompts. The password is still the one they tried.

choices.label: Deny was the whole fix.
Reset it, or they try at 3am.
Approve one so the buzzing ends.

prompt: After a suspected admin compromise, sessions are still open. Resetting the password alone.

choices.label: A new password closes the sessions.
Also revoke the sessions.
Wait for them to time out.

prompt: The vendor says remove full admin in an hour. A reminder is set.

choices.label: An hour cannot do lasting harm.
An hour can leave a door behind.
Sharing your login is safer.

prompt: They will not say which permission the setup needs.

choices.label: Grant full admin until they do.
No list, no access.
Use your account so you can watch.

prompt: The fix is done. The lunch link is sitting in the admin session.

choices.label: Open it. Lunch is not a risk.
Sign out, then open it as yourself.
Leave admin up for the rest of the night.

prompt: Why keep mail off the admin account?

choices.label: Mail is too slow on it.
One bad page would run as admin.
The rule is only for contractors.

prompt: The one-liner has a lot of votes. You have not read it.

choices.label: Votes mean it is safe to paste.
Read it before it runs anywhere.
Run it as a normal user first.

prompt: You read the script. It does more than the fix.

choices.label: Run it. The extra part may help.
Stop. Use the vendor's own fix.
Run it on production only.

prompt: A new admin account appeared that nobody on the team made.

choices.label: Check it in the morning.
Treat it as the incident. Now.
Ask the vendor if it is theirs.

prompt: Access that ends on its own is better than a reminder to remove it because

choices.label: Reminders are slower to click.
Reminders get missed.
A reminder writes a better log.
